newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA WHEAT PRICES FALL ON EXPECTED LOW QUALITY.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA WHEAT PRICES FALL ON EXPECTED LOW QUALITY.

text.p: Bulgarian wheat producers lowered their prices to 240,000 levs per tonne from 250,000 levs in mid-July ex-works on expected low quality due to a delayed harvest and summer rainfall, farm experts said on Friday.

"Producers sell their wheat at 235,000-240,000 levs on expected good wheat output but the delayed harvest and summer rainfalls have seriously affected wheat's quality," Valeria Kostova from state-run Agricultural Market Information System told Reuters.
Rainfall in the Balkan country has not been as serious as in central Europe.
Ultimate wheat harvest deadline in Bulgaria is the end of July.
The Agriculture ministry said on Tuesday Bulgaria had collected some 2.7 million tonnes of wheat from 833,000 hectares harvested so far, which is almost 68 percent of the sown area.
In May, Agriculture Minister Ventsislav Varbanov estimated this year's wheat crop at around 2.4 million tonnes and forecasts were based on an assumed average yield of two tonnes per hectare.
No deals were struck at the Plovdiv and Sofia Commodity Exchanges this week.

"We expect deals around the minimum purchase price as producers have realised that anything above that level is unrealistic and practically unaffordable for buyers," Plovdiv Commodity Exchange chairman Krasimir Dafchev told Reuters.

The minimum purchase price is set at 230,000 levs per tonne from this year's crop in a bid to secure the country's grain balance after excessive wheat exports two years ago and a bad harvest in 1996 caused acute grain shortages earlier this year.
Bulgaria's annual consumption is estimated at 1.6 million tonnes of bread wheat and 800,000 tonnes of feed wheat.
Bulgaria has to export some 232,000 tonnes of wheat this year under futures contracts agreed earlier this year. Poland has said it could accept cash payment for 100,000 of the total.
An export fee of 15 percent of international wheat prices has been also set in a bid to curb exports.
